A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of linear mode connectivity in differentiable tree ensembles. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched, including algorithms relocated from the appendix to the main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 16 tabular datasets, including interpolation accuracies, connectivity barriers, architecture comparisons and split-data model merging.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds decision-list interpolation results and MNIST evaluations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Node weighting, symmetry enumeration, activation/weight matching and the modified decision-list architecture are retained. Algorithms 1–2 move from v1 Appendix A to v2 Section 3.2 with notation edits but unchanged procedural steps. The revised complexity discussion does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST image classification using flattened image inputs (Appendix B, Figures 42–43). This is a limited extension beyond tabular data; the original 16 datasets and full-data/class-skewed split scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Full-data-trained models become explicit reference comparators in split-data test plots, including v2 Figure 8. These references were absent from the corresponding v1 comparisons. The MLP comparison using Git Re-Basin and the existing matching baselines are retained.

E3.justification: The new MNIST evaluation uses flattened inputs with depth 2 and 256 trees. v2 also extends split-data evaluation to ordinary and modified decision lists and introduces full-data test controls. Existing learning rates, batch size, training epochs, interpolation grid and class-split ratios remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 already investigates depth, invariances and decision-list modification. v2 additionally examines ordinary and modified decision-list merging under disjoint, class-skewed training through Figures 30–33 and 38–41. This extends the existing robustness investigation; the additional full-data curves also expose behavior previously summarized by barriers.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the same five random-seed pairs and report standard deviations across five executions. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test or increased run count; additional plots do not establish a changed statistical practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 and 6–13 retain their numerical entries, but v2 substantially expands reported outcomes with decision-list interpolation curves, previously unreported split-data results for both list architectures, full-data reference accuracies and MNIST results. Figures 42–43 show that tree-specific invariances substantially reduce AM interpolation dips on MNIST. These are added results, not improved scores under the original settings.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects v1's claim that LAP must be solved for every invariance pattern, distinguishing a single assignment from pattern enumeration, and explicitly derives U = 2^D D! for oblivious trees. v1 Equation (5), deriving the depth-one ensemble/MLP correspondence, is removed. The central barrier and tree definitions are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the first LMC investigation for soft tree ensembles, the importance of tree-specific invariances, and a modified decision-list architecture requiring only permutation matching. New experiments support these retained claims. Revised application examples do not establish a new central contribution.

C2.justification: The introduction newly links a nearly single symmetry-adjusted basin to robustness against initialization and batch order, while replacing near-functional-equivalence language with near-identical performance. Appendix B explains why full-data references support test comparisons but are unsuitable for analogous training comparisons. Existing deep-tree and computational-efficiency qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v2 Section 4.1 newly states that a reproducible PyTorch implementation is provided in supplementary material; v1 contains no corresponding code-access statement. This is a changed disclosure, although actual code availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs. Existing hardware and implementation settings remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning oblique and soft decision trees, federated learning, general mode connectivity, PyTorch and MNIST. It replaces Mistral 7B with Mixtral of Experts and removes several mixture-of-experts, task-arithmetic and unlearning references. The primary positioning relative to neural-network LMC research remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 expands portions of the introduction and soft-tree explanation, standardizes parameter notation, moves existing algorithms and their notation guide into Section 3.2, revises the conclusion and adds acknowledgments. These are localized editorial and organizational changes within the retained main section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adds a soft-tree schematic, expands the invariance illustration, redraws v1 Figure 5 as grouped bar charts in Figure 6, and adds full-data reference lines to split-data plots. The extensive decision-list and MNIST figure additions substantially expand the graphical presentation. Existing table structures largely remain.

improvement.justification: Full-data test references make the practical model-merging results easier to assess, and the corrected complexity discussion resolves an inconsistency with the existing pseudocode. Added decision-list and MNIST evaluations provide useful validation. These gains outweigh the loss of the short MLP-equivalence derivation, but remain limited: the core findings were already supported in v1, and MNIST-specific protocol details are sparse.
